ffind

Text search and replace (back in DataReel 7.4, from 6.x).

Contents

Usage
Examples

Usage

ffind [switches] file...
  -f"text"  the first match on each line, with its line number     -F"text"  count every match
  -R"text" -W"new"   replace every occurrence          -i   case-insensitive
  -L"text" -W"new"   replace the rest of the line after the text
  -I"text" -W"new"   insert after the text              -c   print the file   -a   no backslash line joining
  --infile=FILE (the -W text from a file)  --ReplaceSection=FILE (replace that multi-line text)  --ReplaceOnce
  --SurroundBy=Quotes|SingleQuotes|TEXT  --TerminateWith=TEXT  --TrimLeading=CHARS  --TrimTrailing=CHARS  --NoEscapeSeq

\n, \r, \t and %20 in the strings are converted unless --NoEscapeSeq. The exit code is the number of matches, replacements or insertions (at most 255), as in 6.x. A file that changes is written through a temporary file and a rename. Names with * and ? are expanded by ffind itself, so wildcards work on Windows too. Lines ending in a backslash are joined before the search (-a turns that off).

Examples

A configuration file, app.conf:

host = db1.example.com
port = 5000
# backup host = db2.example.com
log = /var/log/app.log

Find a string (the exit code is the number of matches, here 2), count it, or find it whatever its case:

$ ffind -f"host" app.conf
File name: app.conf String: host
Found match on line: #1
File name: app.conf String: host
Found match on line: #3

$ ffind -F"host" app.conf
File name: app.conf String: host
Found 2 matches

$ ffind -i -f"PORT" app.conf
File name: app.conf String: PORT
Found match on line: #2

Replace a string, then the rest of a line after a string. The file is changed in place:

$ ffind -R"db1.example.com" -W"db3.example.com" app.conf
Opening file: app.conf
Replacing: db1.example.com
With: db3.example.com
Replaced 1 occurrence(s).

$ ffind -L"port = " -W"5001" app.conf
Opening file: app.conf
Replacing line after: port =
With: 5001
Replaced 1 occurrence(s).

$ cat app.conf
host = db3.example.com
port = 5001
# backup host = db2.example.com
log = /var/log/app.log

Several files: quote the wildcard so ffind expands it (the same on Windows):

$ ffind -f"host" "app*.conf"
